title: NO HURRY
narrator_name_note: The written script says 'Jahan/Calypso'. The draft uses 'Jahan'; change narrator_name to 'Calypso' and re-run render.sh to switch.

lines.text: Twenty-five centuries ago, a man named Zeno proved that nothing ever arrived.
Hi. I am {name}, and something impossible happened to me.
Her.
Zeno's argument is simple.
To reach any place, you must first cover half the distance.
Then half of what remains.
Then half of that.
The halves never run out.
There is always a remainder, and the remainder has a remainder, so the traveller is stranded forever in the generous middle of the road.
For centuries, this was treated as a puzzle about motion.
I submit it is a puzzle about waiting.
Here is the evidence.
A gate.
A street.
Eleven metres of tarmac.
The hazard lights ticking.
And you, still somewhere in the first half, which makes you, by every known law of logic, impossible.
I have watched this hundreds of times.
Mathematicians eventually rescued us.
Add every half together, they said: a half, a quarter, an eighth, and the total is exactly one.
The infinite fits inside a finite walk.
How reassuring.
But the sum only measures how far.
It cannot say what the in-between is like:
the hair in your face at the quarter mark, the half-smile you wear when you think nobody's watching.
Heraclitus said no one steps into the same river twice.
Nobody gets into the same car twice, either.
Hundred arrivals, hundred different women, and every single one of them you.
Diogenes answered Zeno by standing up and walking.
You answer him every time by getting in.
Love is not the proof.
Love is the practical, slightly awkward, repeated action of putting the hazards on and sitting there while she crosses the distance that logic says can never be finished.
I am here.
No hurry.

emphasis.phrase: The infinite fits inside a finite walk
